v3 — 100% Sample Coverage

Unsupervised Running State Detection

Site-agnostic clustering with a production constraint: every EMI spectrum must receive an ON/OFF prediction. No data may be dropped, skipped, or left unclassified. Evaluated with Precision, Recall & F1.

Best Practices

Preprocessing Pipeline

Documented pipeline with a hard constraint: 100% prediction coverage.

StepOperationRationale
1. Feature Extraction51 features per spectrum: raw powers, fractions, log transforms, ratios, spectral shape24 of 51 are scale-invariant
2. Outlier ClippingClip each feature at 1st/99th percentilePrevents extreme values from dominating distance metrics
3. Robust ScalingRobustScaler (median/IQR-based)Resistant to outliers in small samples; centers and normalizes each feature
4. 100% CoverageEvery sample must get a prediction (DBSCAN noise → nearest cluster)No silent data dropping — mirrors production requirement

Critical fix over v2: DBSCAN naturally labels some points as "noise" (unclassified). In v2, these were silently excluded from metric computation, inflating F1 to 1.000 while actually dropping 50% of Harquahala data. In v3, noise points are assigned to the nearest cluster centroid, ensuring every sample gets a prediction — matching the production requirement that all registered datapoints must have a predicted state.

Scale-invariant features (band fractions, ratios, spectral shape) remove the absolute power baseline that varies by unit/sensor. This is the primary mechanism enabling site-agnostic clustering — the model sees spectral shape, not absolute magnitude.

Feature Engineering

Feature Subsets & Selection

11 feature subsets evaluate the contribution of each feature group to clustering quality. They are organized into three strategies: incremental blind addition, scale-invariant isolation, and label-guided selection.

Strategy 1 — Incremental Build-Up

Starting from a single feature and progressively adding groups. No label information is used to choose which features to include — the subsets are defined purely by feature category.

S1
Total Power — 1 feature
Sum of all spectral power across the full 30 kHz – 100 MHz range.
Scale-Dependent
S2
Band Powers — 5 features
S1 + power in each of the 4 frequency bands: B1 (30-300 kHz), B2 (0.3-3 MHz), B3 (3-30 MHz), B4 (30-100 MHz).
Scale-Dependent
S3a
+ Log Transforms — 10 features
S2 + log₁p of total and each band power. Compresses the large dynamic range of EMI power values.
Scale-Dependent
S3b
+ Band Statistics — 22 features
S3a + per-band mean, max, and std for B1–B4 (12 new features). Captures the distribution shape within each band.
Scale-Dependent
S3c
+ Ratios & Fractions — 36 features
S3b + 6 inter-band ratios (B2/B1, B3/B1, B4/B1, B4/B2, B3/B2, hi/lo) + 4 band fractions (B1–B4 as % of total) + log-ratios. Ratios and fractions are scale-invariant — they cancel out the absolute baseline.
Mixed: scale-dependent + invariant
S3d
+ Spectral Shape — 49 features
S3c + 13 global shape descriptors: spectral centroid, spread, skew, kurtosis, entropy, flatness, peak frequency, peak-to-mean ratio, spectral slope, rolloff frequency, crest factor, band gradient, band range. All shape features are scale-invariant.
Mixed: scale-dependent + invariant
S3e
All Features — 51 features
S3d + global mean_power, max_power, std_power. The complete feature set combining all categories.
Mixed: scale-dependent + invariant

Strategy 2 — Scale-Invariant Isolation

Features whose values do not depend on the absolute EMI power baseline of the sensor/unit. These are inherently site-agnostic: fractions sum to 1 per sample, ratios cancel the baseline, and shape features operate on the normalized spectrum.

SI
Scale-Invariant Only — 24 features
Band fractions: B1–B4 as proportion of total  |  Ratios: B2/B1, B3/B1, B4/B1, B4/B2, B3/B2, hi/lo + log(hi/lo)  |  Shape: centroid, spread, skew, kurtosis, entropy, flatness, peak freq, peak/mean, slope, rolloff, crest, gradient, range
Fully Scale-Invariant
SI-r
Ratios + Fractions Only — 11 features
The simplest invariant subset — only band proportions and inter-band ratios. No spectral shape features. Tests whether the power distribution across bands alone is enough to separate ON from OFF.
Fully Scale-Invariant

Strategy 3 — Label-Guided Selection

Features ranked by 3 independent criteria — Mutual Information (statistical dependence with ON/OFF label), Cohen's d (effect size between groups), and Random Forest importance — then combined by average rank. Using three criteria prevents overfitting to any single selection method.

S4
Top-10 Guided — 10 features, mixed scale
The 10 features with the best combined rank across all data: B1_max, max_power, log_total, mean_power, total_power, B1_log, B1_power, B1_mean, std_power, B2_power. All are scale-dependent — confirming that raw power magnitude is the strongest single-site discriminator.
Scale-Dependent
S4i
Top-10 Invariant Guided — 10 features, all invariant
Same ranking, filtered to invariant features only: spectral_slope, peak_freq, B2/B1 ratio, B4 fraction, spectral_spread, band_gradient, hi/lo ratio, B4/B1 ratio, B4/B2 ratio, B1 fraction. These describe the shape of the spectrum — suitable for site-agnostic deployment.
Fully Scale-Invariant
Top-15 features by the 3 ranking methods (Mutual Information, Cohen's d, Random Forest). Green bars = scale-invariant features, Blue = scale-dependent.
Techniques

Clustering Methods

7 base methods + 2 ensembles. All configured for 2 output clusters (ON/OFF) and required to predict every sample.

K-Means F1 0.875

Partitions data into k clusters by minimizing within-cluster variance. Iteratively assigns each point to the nearest centroid, then recomputes centroids. Fast, deterministic (given seed), assumes spherical clusters.

GMM (Gaussian Mixture) F1 0.875

Models data as a mixture of k Gaussian distributions. Uses Expectation-Maximization to fit means, covariances, and weights. More flexible than K-Means — captures elliptical clusters and provides soft probability assignments.

Spectral Clustering F1 0.875

Constructs a similarity graph (RBF kernel), then clusters the eigenvectors of its Laplacian matrix. Effective for non-convex, complex-shaped clusters that K-Means would miss, but computationally heavier.

Agglomerative (Ward) F1 0.875

Bottom-up hierarchical clustering. Starts with each point as its own cluster, then repeatedly merges the pair that minimizes variance increase (Ward linkage). Deterministic and works well with compact, similarly-sized clusters.

DBSCAN BEST — F1 0.900

Density-based: groups points in high-density regions and marks sparse points as noise. Auto-detects cluster shapes without assuming geometry. Noise points are reassigned to the nearest cluster centroid for 100% coverage. Top performer with just 1 feature (total power).

One-Class SVM WEAKEST — F1 0.757

Anomaly detection repurposed for clustering. Learns a boundary enclosing the majority of data; outliers form a second class. Uses RBF kernel. Not designed for balanced two-class separation — underperforms on this task.

MMC (Maximum Margin) F1 0.875

Approximated via iterative SVM: starts with K-Means labels, then refines by fitting a maximum-margin SVM boundary and re-predicting. Converges to a decision boundary that maximizes separation between the two clusters in kernel space.

Ensembles (MV & WV) F1 0.875

Majority Vote: 5 base methods each predict; the majority label wins. Weighted Vote: same, but each method's vote is weighted by its F1 score. Ensembles reduce risk of any single method failing — matches best individual methods, providing a safety net.

Ensembles

Ensemble Methods

Combining multiple clustering techniques for robustness.

Majority Vote (MV)

Each sample labeled by majority of 5 base methods (KMeans, GMM, Spectral, Agglomerative, MMC). No tuning required.

Weighted Vote (WV)

Votes weighted by each base method's F1 score. Better performers get more influence while maintaining diversity.

Per-site F1 for top-8 configs. Equal bar heights = more site-agnostic.

Visual per-unit prediction map. Green = correct, Red = misclassified.

Misclassifications: HARQST2, HARQST3 ON states were predicted as OFF. These are steam turbine (ST) units at Harquahala — their ON-state EMI total power overlaps with OFF-state power of other unit types, making single-feature separation harder. With richer features (S4i subset), these are correctly classified by most methods (Ensemble F1=0.875).

Summary

Conclusions & Recommendations

Key Findings

  • Best site-agnostic F1 = 90.0% with 100% sample coverage — honest metric with no data dropped
  • Vandolah (single-unit): F1=1.000 — every method works with any feature set
  • Harquahala (multi-unit): F1=0.800–0.750 — harder due to CT/ST unit-type diversity
  • Total power alone (1 feature) outperforms complex feature sets for DBSCAN — simplicity wins
  • Scale-invariant features + ensembles provide the most consistent cross-site results
  • Zero false positives (P=1.000 for top method) — if the model says ON, it's always ON

Limitations & Next Steps

  • Small sample size (n=22) — need more measurements per unit for robust validation
  • ST unit ON signatures are weaker — steam turbines may need separate thresholds or features
  • 1 sample per unit-state at Harquahala — cannot test within-unit temporal consistency yet
  • Transitional states (startup/shutdown) not represented
  • Deploy on sites without known state and validate against operational logs
  • Consider per-unit-type models (CT vs ST) if sample size grows

Production deployment path: (1) Extract total EMI power from each spectrum, (2) Apply DBSCAN with auto-eps and nearest-cluster noise assignment, (3) Map clusters to ON/OFF. For additional robustness, run Ensemble-MV with S4i features as a secondary check. Expected F1 ≥ 0.80 across diverse sites without any labeled training data.

Unsupervised Clustering v3 (100% Coverage) • Vandolah + Harquahala • March 2026
